chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
When you face the qiblah with your face, then do not turn your face away from the qiblah, lest your salat (prayer) be invalidated.
For Allah, Exalted is He, said to His Prophet عليه السلام concerning the obligatory prayer:
So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it.
And lower your gaze humbly, and do not raise it to the sky; rather, keep it before your face at the place of your sajdah (prostration).

key_terms.اخْشَعْ: be humble and subdued, referring to reverent attentiveness in prayer
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ: the Sacred Mosque in Makkah, the direction of qiblah
key_terms.بَصَرَكَ: your gaze or eyesight during prayer
key_terms.صَلَاتُكَ: your salat (prayer), whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.مَوْضِعِ سُجُودِكَ: the place of your prostration, where the gaze should be directed
key_terms.وُجُوهَكُمْ: your faces, indicating bodily orientation in prayer

ai.seo_question: Does turning the face away from the qiblah invalidate salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling and etiquette for salat (prayer): one must remain facing the qiblah and not turn the face away in a manner that invalidates the prayer. It also cites the Quranic command to face al-Masjid al-Haram and instructs the worshipper to maintain khushu' by lowering the gaze toward the place of sajdah.
